newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.20 firmer.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.20 firmer.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.20 cent firmer Tuesday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, dealers said.
NYCE's weekly spec/hedge report showed the speculators to be holding a 19.5 percent net short position, up slightly from 19.3 percent last week.

Market sources had been anticipating a shortcovering rally but recent weakness gives the funds little incentive to cover positions. Prices could continue to slide, hitting new life-of-contract lows, before turning around, they said.
A total of 709 notices have been issued to date, NYCE said.
USDA said Monday that 25 percent of the U.S. cotton crop has been planted, compared with 31 percent a year ago and 37 percent in a five-year average.
Rain and cold weather in the Delta, parts of Texas and in North Carolina, have slowed planting progress.

Monday, most-active July cotton ended 0.50 cent weaker at 71.90 cents per lb after trading from 72.95 to 71.50 cents, a life-of-contract low. New-crop December finished down 0.11 cent at 74.82 cents, while the rest of the board ended 0.20 to 0.05 lower.
